title: Pixel 11 battery drain could have an unexpected culprit: Your Wi-Fi router
summary: Tests point to a router-specific sleep issue, but the cause isn't confirmed.
body: TL;DR Some Pixel 11 owners are reporting excessive idle battery drain, with Wi-Fi showing unusually high battery usage. A detailed test found that certain routers repeatedly woke the phone, preventing it from sleeping properly. Switching to Wi-Fi 5 or another router dramatically improved battery life, but the exact cause remains unconfirmed. Pixel owners are no strangers to battery-life complaints , and Google’s Tensor era has had its share of heat, modem, and efficiency problems. The Pixel 11 series looked like a step forward, especially with its new MediaTek modem, but some owners are now chasing a different kind of drain. A detailed Reddit investigation suggests certain Wi-Fi routers may be keeping Pixel 11 phones awake far more often than they should. Reddit user Albamen13 noticed their Pixel 11 Pro XL losing roughly 2.5% to 3% battery per hour while sitting idle on Wi-Fi. Using BetterBatteryStats, they found that Wi-Fi activity was waking the phone about 135 times per minute, preventing it from properly going to sleep for 59% to 67% of the test.

title: Gmail just made copying 2FA codes much less annoying

body: TL;DR Gmail is rolling out a “Copy code” button for two-factor authentication emails on Android and iOS. The shortcut lets you copy a verification code directly from your inbox without opening the email. The feature is appearing in Gmail for Android version 2026.09.07.x and iOS version 6.0.260907, but not on the web yet. Gmail has already made email easier to navigate this month with Live voice features and Gemini-powered inbox answers , and now Google is shaving another few seconds off a common task. Gmail is rolling out a new “Copy code” shortcut that lets you grab a 2FA code straight from the inbox without opening the message first. While two-factor authentication is supposed to keep your accounts safer, the last step can still feel unnecessarily clumsy when the code lands in your inbox. This shortcut is here to address that, and it appears as a pill-shaped “Copy code: 000000” button beneath the email’s subject line, in the same area Gmail uses for attachment previews and other contextual actions.

title: Google Discover now wants you to read and see less of the actual internet

body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Google is testing a new feature called “Dive deeper” in Google Discover. The new experience can also surface links to related stories, community reactions, and original reporting if you want to explore further. For users, it could make Discover more convenient, but it may also mean fewer people actually open the publisher articles that appear in their feeds. Google Discover is testing a new way to make you learn more about the stories appearing in your feed, and it could mean you spend less time actually reading what your favorite websites are reporting and watching videos from the creators you like.
